steps.question: Do the counts.csv (12000 genes x 7 sample columns) and metadata.csv (6 samples, condition: treated/control) align, and are there sample-level anomalies (outliers, low library size, or mislabeling) that would compromise a 3-vs-3 comparison?
acceptance_criteria: Reports which sample columns in counts.csv match the 6 sample IDs in metadata.csv and explicitly flags any extra/unmatched column
Computes library size (total counts) per sample and flags any sample with a library size markedly discordant from the group mean
Produces a PCA or hierarchical clustering plot on variance-stabilized/log-CPM values labeled by condition (treated vs control) to check that replicates cluster by group
Produces a sample-sample correlation heatmap
States explicitly that with n=3/group, no single QC step can be used to justify discarding a sample without strong cause, since doing so would drop power further

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression, treated vs control
caveats: Must probe for DESeq2/apeglm/ashr availability before use and degrade to edgeR if absent — package presence is unconfirmed for this environment
n=3/group is the minimum DESeq2 supports for dispersion estimation; do not overstate confidence in the dispersion fit
Unpaired single-batch design means no batch term is needed, but this should be stated as an assumption from the metadata, not silently assumed
steps.question: Which of the ~12000 liver genes are differentially expressed between drug-treated (n=3) and control (n=3) samples, using a negative-binomial model appropriate for raw Salmon gene-level counts?
acceptance_criteria: Uses DESeq2 (or, if unavailable, edgeR) with a design of ~condition (treated vs control) on raw integer counts, confirmed to be the reconciled sample set from T1S1
Reports size-factor normalization, dispersion estimates, and confirms the negative-binomial dispersion fit is stable given n=3 per group
Applies independent filtering and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction; reports gene counts at FDR<0.05, FDR<0.1, and nominal p<0.05 thresholds separately so the FDR-vs-nominal gap at low n is visible
Applies log fold-change shrinkage (apeglm or ashr if available, otherwise normal shrinkage) and reports shrunken LFC alongside raw LFC
Outputs a full results table (gene, baseMean, log2FoldChange, shrunken LFC, p-value, padj) and a volcano plot

Explicitly reports that with 3 replicates per group, statistical power is limited to genes with large effect sizes and low within-group variance; states the estimated minimum detectable fold change is not formally computed here but flags this as a known limitation of n=3 designs
If DESeq2 is unavailable, falls back to edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test and states this substitution explicitly in the output

steps.name: Power and confidence assessment for the n=3 design
caveats: Post-hoc power/stability analysis cannot substitute for a priori power calculation and must not be reported as such
Leave-one-out resampling at n=3 leaves only n=2 in the held-out group, which itself has very limited power — frame results as qualitative robustness signal, not a formal power estimate
steps.question: Given only 3 replicates per group, how much confidence can be placed in the DE calls from T1S2 — what fold-change/variance regime was this study powered to detect, and how stable are the significance calls?
acceptance_criteria: Reports the empirical coefficient of variation / dispersion distribution across genes from the DESeq2 fit and relates it to expected detectable fold-change at n=3 (e.g., via a power curve or dispersion-vs-power reference, using standard RNA-seq power relationships)

Performs a leave-one-out or jackknife-style resampling (dropping one sample at a time from the 3-vs-3 design where at least 2 remain per group) to report how stable the top DE gene list is to removal of any single replicate, as a direct empirical check on n=3 fragility

Explicitly states in output that formal a priori power calculations were not part of the original experimental design and that this step assesses achieved/post-hoc confidence only, which is inherently limited
Summarizes, in plain terms, which DE calls are robust (survive resampling, large effect, low dispersion) versus fragile (sensitive to single-sample removal)

steps.name: Pathway enrichment on DE gene list
caveats: Must confirm a human-specific gene set collection is actually available before committing to a specific database name in output
Do not treat enrichment significance as adding independent statistical confidence beyond what the DE analysis already established
steps.question: Are the genes differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples enriched for specific biological pathways or gene sets, and how should that enrichment be interpreted given the small underlying gene list from an n=3 design?
acceptance_criteria: Runs over-representation or gene set enrichment analysis on the DESeq2 results from T1S2 (using FDR<0.1 gene list for over-representation, and the full ranked gene list by shrunken LFC/stat for GSEA/fgsea) against a human gene set collection (e.g., Hallmark, GO, Reactome) confirmed present in the environment before use
If no human pathway gene set reference is available in the environment, explicitly reports that enrichment could not be run and states this as a gap rather than fabricating pathway results
Reports enriched terms with FDR-adjusted enrichment p-values, not raw p-values
States explicitly that enrichment run on a DE list derived from n=3/group carries the same power limitations as the upstream DE call, and results should be treated as hypothesis-generating

plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control DE analysis (n=3/group)
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq raw gene-level counts from Salmon (12000 genes x 7 samples file, but metadata lists 6 samples: 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch) in human liver tissue under drug treatment. With only n=3 per group, a standard negative-binomial GLM (DESeq2) is the right statistical model for count data at this scale, but power is inherently limited: at n=3/group, only genes with large, consistent fold changes will reach significance after multiple-testing correction, and moderate effects will be missed (false negatives). The plan therefore (1) reconciles the counts file's 7 columns against the 6-sample metadata before any modeling, (2) runs QC/exploratory diagnostics (library size, PCA, sample correlation) to catch outliers or mislabeling that would be catastrophic at this sample size, (3) fits DESeq2 with a two-group design and shrunken log fold changes, (4) explicitly quantifies statistical power/confidence given n=3 via dispersion diagnostics, independent filtering, and reporting of both nominal and FDR-adjusted results with effect-size shrinkage, and (5) contextualizes any significant DE genes with pathway enrichment, flagging that enrichment on a small, possibly underpowered gene list should be read as hypothesis-generating. Every step is explicit that n=3/group limits confidence and that results should be treated as a discovery-phase, not confirmatory, analysis.
